- Core policy read: The FOMC paused at 5.25–5.50% and continued QT, emphasizing data dependence and persistent inflation risks—hawkish on balance.
- SLOOS overlay (July 2023): Banks reported broad-based tightening of lending standards and terms across C&I (including IG and below-IG, syndicated and non-syndicated), CRE (construction, land development, nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily), RRE (GSE-eligible, jumbo, government, QM and non-QM), HELOCs, and consumer credit (credit cards, auto). Loan demand also weakened in several segments (e.g., subprime mortgages).
- Implications: The SLOOS confirms and amplifies the statement’s warning that tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity, hiring, and inflation. This adds downside growth risk and reinforces a cautious stance despite solid current activity and low unemployment.
- Net tone: Cautiously hawkish and risk-aware, skewed more negative than a neutral read due to widespread credit tightening and weaker demand evident in SLOOS.
